detailed_rationale:
Century Plyboards is the organized plywood market leader in India (~29% share), and the latest data shows a genuine demand recovery: TTM sales growth of ~23% (a reacceleration versus the quant sheet's 3-year CAGR of ~14%), with operating margins holding stable at ~13%. This corroborates the growth_3y_score of 54 in the quant sheet and suggests real market-share and/or category-demand tailwinds (plywood/laminates benefiting from real-estate and renovation demand, plus a likely continued organized-versus-unorganized formalization shift, a dynamic common to several building-materials categories in this batch).

The central concern, and the one genuinely worth engaging as the strongest bear point, is balance-sheet leverage: total borrowings have more than doubled in two years, from Rs.771cr (Mar 2024) to Rs.1,765cr (Mar 2026), and TTM interest expense has surged to Rs.113cr. The company's own results commentary explicitly attributes volatile net profit growth to this rising interest burden -- i.e., revenue and operating margins are genuinely fine, but profit growth is being diluted by the cost of debt-funded expansion (fixed assets have grown to Rs.2,813cr, consistent with capacity investment rather than distress borrowing, but a real drag on bottom-line growth nonetheless).

Return on equity (~11.5% three-year average) is respectable but not exceptional for a ~57.5x earnings multiple and ~6.8x book value -- a rich valuation for the demonstrated (debt-diluted) profit growth. Low dividend payout (~8% of FY26 profit) is consistent with continued capacity-expansion reinvestment.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite is Hold (45.1/3yr). Fundamentals support an unchanged Hold: genuine demand recovery and market leadership, offset by a real and rising leverage/interest-cost drag on profit growth and a valuation that is not cheap for the current return profile. No basis for escalation -- this is a normal growth-versus-leverage trade-off, not a data blind spot.
summary: Century Plyboards is India's leading organized plywood maker and is seeing a genuine demand recovery, but debt has more than doubled in two years to fund capacity expansion, and rising interest costs are now diluting profit growth even as revenue holds up well. At a rich valuation for this profile, we rate it a hold.
positive_para: Clear market leadership (~29% share of the organized plywood market) with a genuine recent demand recovery (TTM sales growth ~23%) and stable operating margins (~13%), supported by ongoing capacity investment (fixed assets now Rs.2,813cr) that should support future volume growth.
negative_para: Total debt has more than doubled in two years (Rs.771cr to Rs.1,765cr) and TTM interest expense has surged to Rs.113cr, with the company's own commentary attributing volatile net profit growth directly to this rising interest burden -- a genuine and worsening drag on bottom-line growth even as revenue and margins look healthy. At ~57.5x earnings and ~6.8x book value for an ~11.5% ROE, the valuation leaves little room for the leverage trend to worsen further.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~57.5x earnings and ~6.8x book value for ~11.5% ROE with rising interest costs actively diluting profit growth, the multiple prices in continued strong revenue growth translating cleanly to the bottom line -- a scenario the current leverage trend is working against. Rich rather than cheap; the growth story is real, but the debt-funded capex is a genuine and current cost to it.
